wars.outcome: Karib'il Watar of Saba destroyed Awsan in the late 7th century BCE; 'Saba, after defeating Awsan, divided the territory between two of its other allies at the time', Qataban and Hadhramaut.
wars.note: Qataban's share is not given and Awsan (centred on the Wadi Markha) is not in Cliopatria, so no zone and no gain event; years are a reading of 'late 7th century'. Awsan later 'experienced a resurgence and regained its autonomy' (2nd century BC per Robin, 1st per Schiettecatte).

wars.name: Qatabanian coalition against the Sabaeans

wars.name: Aelius Gallus's expedition to Arabia
wars.outcome: The Romans 'attempted to conquer Saba around 26/25 BCE' and gave up the siege of Marib because of 'heat exhaustion'; no border moved.

notes:
Page budget: 5 pages (Qataban, Sabaeans, History of Yemen, Awsan, Himyarite Kingdom). The Qataban article has no area, no reign dates and few year-level dates, so most events carry confidence 1 or 2.

Cliopatria rows: (1) the first shape starts in -350 but the page has a centralised state from the late 7th/early 6th century BCE: new keyframes for -625..-551 and -420..-351, with the years -550..-421 left empty (Qataban under Saba, matching the Sabaean dossier's gain/loss). (2) The -350 shape (11,920 km2) is only the Wadi Bayhan core; the page's maximum extent reaches the Bab al-Mandab, so it is adjusted to the core plus Cliopatria's first Himyarite shape (land 'integrated into the Qatabanian kingdom until 110 BCE'). (3) No Qataban shape for -66..153: the core is kept (the pages show the kingdom alive in the 1st century BCE, 26 BCE and until the late 1st/2nd century CE), which overlaps the himyarite-kingdom shapes -66..153 (334,765 and 149,074 km2; checked by intersection, about 12,500 km2 of the core); the Himyar group must decide. (4) The end 183 is the last Cliopatria shape; the prose of the page says late 1st century CE.

Disagreements: end of Qataban (late 1st century CE in the prose, 'late 1st or late 2nd century CE' in the infobox, c. 200 CE on the Himyar page, 'collapse of Qataban in 50 BC' on History of Yemen); the Himyar page says both that Qataban was conquered c. 200 CE and that Saba and Qataban 'split from the Kingdom of Ḥimyar' in the early 2nd century AD.

Not settled (page silent): the year of Qataban's conquest of Ma'in (see the Minaeans dossier); Qataban's share of Awsan (late 7th century); the year of the expansion to the Bab al-Mandab; the line between Hadramawt and Himyar at the end. The Sabaean dossier lacks the loss matching the -350 gain and a vassal_start for Qataban in -550..-421.

Counterparts needing dossiers: Awsan (Wadi Markha; destroyed late 7th century BCE, resurgent 2nd/1st century BCE). Region names: none needed beyond Cliopatria shapes; place name Timna' (capital) is missing from the gazetteer.
